content: Ezetimibe is a medication prescribed to help reduce cholesterol and other fatty substances in the blood. It is typically used in conjunction with lifestyle changes, such as adopting a healthy diet, losing weight, and engaging in regular exercise. This medication can be taken alone or in combination with a statin, which is an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor. Ezetimibe belongs to a class of drugs known as cholesterol-lowering medications. It works by inhibiting the absorption of cholesterol in the intestine. The accumulation of cholesterol and fats along the walls of blood vessels, a condition called atherosclerosis, can restrict blood flow and reduce the oxygen supply to vital organs such as the heart and brain. By lowering blood cholesterol and fat levels, ezetimibe may reduce the risk of developing heart disease, angina (chest pain), strokes, and heart attacks. In addition to taking this medication, making specific changes to daily habits, such as eating a diet low in saturated fat and cholesterol, exercising for at least 30 minutes most days, and losing weight if overweight, can further help lower cholesterol levels. Ezetimibe is available as an oral tablet and is usually taken once daily, with or without food. To ensure consistent use, it is recommended to take it at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take ezetimibe exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its additional applications, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting ezetimibe, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention anticoagulants (blood thinners) like warfarin, cyclosporine, fenofibrate, and gemfibrozil, as these may require dose adjustments or careful monitoring for side effects. If you are taking bile acid sequestrants such as cholestyramine, colesevelam, or colestipol, take them either four hours before or two hours after ezetimibe. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of liver disease or if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking ezetimibe, contact your doctor immediately. To support the effectiveness of ezetimibe, follow a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet. This includes foods like cottage cheese, fat-free milk, fish (not canned in oil), vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils and margarines (e.g., corn, safflower, canola, and soybean oils). Avoid foods high in fat, such as fatty meats, liver, egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, shortening, lard, pastries, cakes, cookies, gravy, peanut butter, chocolate, olives, potato chips, coconut, cheese (other than cottage cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, and fried foods. If you miss a dose of ezetimibe, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Ezetimibe may cause side effects. Common, less severe side effects include headache, dizziness, diarrhea, sore throat, runny nose, sneezing, and joint pain. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though uncommon, require immediate medical attention. These include hives, rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs, hoarseness, upset stomach, extreme tiredness, unusual bleeding or bruising, lack of energy, loss of appetite, pain in the upper right part of the stomach, yellowing of the skin or eyes, flu-like symptoms, muscle pain or weakness, fever, chills, pale or fatty stools, and chest pain. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Store ezetimibe in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order tests before and during treatment to monitor your response to ezetimibe. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
